identification.name: Titanium Ti-6Al-4V (Annealed)
identification.common_form_notes: Widely available from aerospace metal distributors as AMS 4928 bar, AMS 4911 sheet/plate, and AMS 4928 billet. Machining requires sharp carbide tooling, low cutting speeds, and flood coolant to manage low thermal conductivity and work-hardening tendency.
identification.notes: Ti-6Al-4V (UNS R56400, also written Ti 6-4) is the most widely used titanium alloy, accounting for ~50% of global titanium production. Properties given are for the fully annealed condition per AMS 4928. Thermal conductivity is very low (~1/6 that of steel) — this governs machining practice and is a design consideration for heat-dissipating structures. Do not use for sustained structural loads above ~315 °C as strength falls off significantly. Corrosion resistance is excellent in most environments (seawater, acids, body fluids) due to a stable TiO₂ surface layer — avoid contact with liquid oxygen, red fuming nitric acid, and chlorine at elevated temperatures. Biocompatible per ISO 5832-3. Shear strength derived from von Mises criterion: UTS/√3 = 950/√3 ≈ 549 MPa. Cryogenic k(T) and CTE(T) table data from NIST Cryogenic Materials Database (nist-cryo-ti64); CTE table values are instantaneous coefficients derived from NIST polynomial fits.

typical_usage: Aerospace primary structures (airframe brackets, engine mounts, fan blades); biomedical implants (orthopaedic stems, bone screws, dental implants); marine hardware and fasteners in salt water; high-performance automotive and motorsport components; chemical processing equipment in corrosive environments; sports equipment (bicycle frames, golf club heads).
